sourceNotes: CrUX API: p75 and good/NI/poor shares of real Chrome users over the 28-day collection period 2026-10-13..2026-11-09. https://developer.chrome.com/docs/crux/api
CrUX History API: 25 weekly 28-day periods, oldest first; ineligible periods are null. https://developer.chrome.com/docs/crux/history-api

PageSpeed Insights loadingExperience/originLoadingExperience (analysed 2026-11-11T11:05:02.524Z / 2026-11-11T11:06:58.731Z): separate source next to CrUX, reports no collection period. https://developers.google.com/speed/docs/insights/rest/v5/pagespeedapi/runpagespeed
CrUX history PHONE url https://edition.cnn.com/2026/11/04/science/southern-taurids-meteor-shower: 24 of 25 periods ineligible (kept as null).
CrUX history DESKTOP url https://edition.cnn.com/2026/11/04/science/southern-taurids-meteor-shower: 24 of 25 periods ineligible (kept as null).
CrUX PHONE vs PSI mobile, url level: identical (p75 115 ms, same good/NI/poor shares).
CrUX PHONE vs PSI mobile, origin level: identical (p75 180 ms, same good/NI/poor shares).
CrUX DESKTOP vs PSI desktop, url level: identical (p75 60 ms, same good/NI/poor shares).
CrUX DESKTOP vs PSI desktop, origin level: identical (p75 89 ms, same good/NI/poor shares).

reconciliation.text: Field INP p75 (CrUX PHONE, url level, 2026-10-13..2026-11-09) = 115 ms. No lab scenario reached it: not reproduced in the lab (real devices, logged-in states, iframes, untested interactions).

limitations: Lab values are "lab @ CPU 4x, mobile emulation, headless Chrome Chrome/155.0.8059.39" on one machine - not INP. INP is the CrUX field p75 above.

CrUX INP is the 75th percentile over 28 days of real Chrome users' page loads, each load's INP being its worst interaction minus one per 50 (https://developers.google.com/speed/docs/insights/v5/about, https://web.dev/articles/inp#what-is-inp).
Only interactions the tool discovered and could trigger safely were measured; logged-in states, real form input, ads and cross-origin iframes were not.
First-party mutating requests were blocked and cross-document navigations answered with 204, so work that depends on those responses is not measured.
GPU/raster work is not CPU-throttled by Chrome's CPU throttling; presentation delay on real mid-tier phones can be larger.
